hard_fails.actual: Resolving a dispute as 'In Favor of Buyer' (or 'Full Refund') writes the order to status=refunded with refunded_amount = full order total BEFORE the actual gateway refund is attempted. On order #36 (payment_method=standalone), the gateway refund call failed ('Auto-refund FAILED for order 36: gateway standalone not available or missing process_refund(). The buyer has NOT been refunded.' - debug.log 06:34:34) and the vendor earnings reversal was also skipped ('no completed wallet credit found for the vendor, so the earnings reversal is skipped'). The order and dispute both now read as fully resolved/refunded in the admin UI - Dispute #8 shows status Resolved, resolution favor_buyer - with no visible error anywhere, while the buyer never received their money back. Root cause: WPSellServices\Services\OrderService::apply_refund_status() (src/Services/OrderService.php:281) writes `refunded_amount` to the DB unconditionally before the status transition/gateway hook runs, and DisputeService::resolve()/handle_resolution() treats apply_refund_status()'s return value (which reflects only the DB write + status transition, not the gateway call) as success.

top3: BLOCK: Resolving a dispute in favor of the buyer (or Full Refund) marks the order 'refunded' with the full amount recorded in refunded_amount, even when the underlying gateway refund silently fails - debug.log proves 'Auto-refund FAILED ... The buyer has NOT been refunded' on order #36, yet the admin UI and DB both show a clean resolved/refunded state with no error surfaced anywhere. A site owner would believe every dispute they resolve this way has actually paid the buyer back when it may not have.

Priority A is now HALF fixed. Unpublishing a service already in a buyer's cart now shows a clear, correctly-named notice ('...cannot be ordered right now: This service is not currently available. Remove it to continue.') and checkout is genuinely refused server-side (WooCommerce Store API returns 409, verified via network trace, no wpss_orders row created) - this closes last cycle's hard_fail cleanly, at both 1280 and 390. But deleting the same cart item instead produces NO notice at all - the item just vanishes and the cart reads 'Your cart is currently empty!' with zero explanation, which a real buyer would read as a bug, not as 'that service is gone.'

The Cloud Storage 'Test Connection' button (Settings -> Advanced) never shows the admin anything. Instrumentation proves the click handler fires, the AJAX round-trip completes, the server returns a correct message either way ('This provider does not support connection testing.' for S3, or a client-side guard for Local), and the JS response handler calls showNotice() with the right arguments - but no toast or notice ever appears in the DOM. An admin configuring cloud storage gets no feedback whatsoever from this button, success or failure.

failures.triage_note: Half-regression of the same feature area as last cycle's hard_fail. The unpublish path (StandaloneProductProvider/WooCommerceAdapter's new availability check) fires a clear cart notice; the delete path removes the WooCommerce cart item (product post presumably force-deleted alongside, or the line silently drops on cart validation) but never routes through the same 'this service is not currently available' notice path, so the buyer gets no explanation at all.

failures.actual: As wpss_buyer_ella: after force-deleting service 238 while it sat alone in her cart, /cart-2/ rendered the generic empty-cart state ('Your cart is currently empty!') with no notice of any kind, at 1280px. failures.triage_note: wp-sell-services-pro/assets/js/admin.js:632-661 binds #wpss-test-storage-connection's click handler, correctly early-guards on provider==='local' (calling showStorageNotice('error', ...)), and otherwise posts action=wpss_pro_test_storage via $.post, routing the response through showStorageNotice() -> WPSSPro.showNotice() -> window.wpssToast(). Confirmed via a runtime spy that showNotice IS invoked with the correct (type, message) pair in both the local-guard case and the real S3 AJAX-response case (server correctly replies {success:false, data:{message:'This provider does not support connection testing.'}}), and confirmed window.wpssToast works fine when invoked directly from the console (creates a visible .wpss-toast element) - but no .wpss-toast element, and no legacy .notice fallback element, ever appears in the DOM when the real call chain runs. Needs a JS-side debugging session to find where the toast call is being lost between showNotice() and DOM insertion in this specific call path.
failures.expected: Per S4.1: the connection test result (pass or a clear failure reason) is shown to the admin.
failures.actual: Clicking Test Connection with Storage Provider = Local (WordPress Media Library) produces zero visible feedback. Switching to Amazon S3 (no credentials) and clicking Test Connection completes a real AJAX round trip with a correct error message server-side, but again zero visible feedback in the browser - no toast, no notice, nothing changes on screen.
